To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a hierarchical classification network with multilayer dense connections is able to learn the hierarchical structure of concepts with a minimal increase in network capacity, while maintaining the categorical accuracy; (2) the proposed network can be trained end-to-end, and can predict the conceptual class of the input image, along with the categorical class.

(1) a single dense connection layer can predict the conceptual class in a hierarchical order with minimal increase in the network size while maintaining categorical accuracy; (2) a multilayer of dense connections can be used to predict a hierarchical classification with higher accuracy and minimal increase in network parameters.

(i) we propose a multilayers dense connectivity for a convolutional neural network that can simultaneously predict the category and its conceptual superclasses; (ii) we demonstrate that our proposed architecture, in conjunction with convolutional feature layers from a popular CNN, can learn to predict conceptual classes with minimal addition to the network size while maintaining categorical classification accuracy; and (iii) we demonstrate the utility of this architecture for hierarchical classification tasks in the domain of natural scene understanding

the following questions.
the question of how to learn a multilayer hierarchy of concepts from images, where the concepts are defined by their hierarchical relations and where each concept has a corresponding set of images.
